title: Outgoing user-notification / messaging backbone
description: Datum has no outbound messaging surface to communicate with users. Design: typed Notice record in gui-protocol (id/source/severity/category/title/body/actions/condition/timestamp), presented by the shell as three tiers — transient toasts (bottom-right, auto-expire), sticky condition-banners (KiCad-infobar style, auto-clear when condition resolves), and a persistent Notices log behind a status-bar bell. Publishers state facts; shell decides presentation. Never journaled (consumer/env state, not a design mutation). Headless surfaces render same notices as text/JSON. Optional chime on warning+ severity, globally disableable, redundant with icon/color/text (accessibility). Shared-by-construction backbone, not a one-off dialog. Weave into UI_LAYOUT_SYSTEM_CONTRACT or a decision record + PROGRESS/Frontier.

title: DWT: notify user KDE 'disable touchpad while typing' blocks Space-drag pan
description: KDE Wayland default 'Disable while typing' suppresses touchpad motion whenever a key (incl. held Space) is down, blocking the Space+left-drag pan gesture. First client of the notification backbone: condition-bound sticky banner. Startup probe parses ~/.config/kcminputrc [Libinput][vid][pid][dev] groups — key DisableWhileTyping is ABSENT at the blocking default (present only once user unchecks it), so absence=trap-live is a deterministic signal. Escalate severity if no external mouse is enumerated (touchpad is the only pan device). Action button launches 'systemsettings kcm_touchpad'. Banner auto-clears when probe sees the fix. GNOME sibling adapter later (gsettings org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.touchpad disable-while-typing).

(6) TF-02 correction: the shell CONTENT area needs its own hit target (focus + selection anchor); activity rows must NOT be terminal-entry targets. (7) Source health: keyboard_focus.rs at 606/700 — TF-02..05 must extract cohesively, not accumulate. Sequence: corrections 1-5 BEFORE resuming TF-02..05. Owner is the human-interface authority; all of this dispositioned by owner review, not agent judgment.

comments.text: OWNER DECISION (2026-08-14): the epic's underspecified middle (custom grid / width / reflow / polish phases) is REPLACED by (a) a FEATURE-COMPLETE contract per the seven-point directive above, and (b) an ADOPTION-FIRST core boundary — a mature terminal core (alacritty_terminal first candidate; libghostty-vt fallback evaluation) behind Datum's own renderer adapter, rather than a homegrown cell-grid state model. RETAINED: portable-pty layer, Datum-native rendering + chrome + interaction conventions, the existing terminal context pipeline (sanctioned back-door), and the swappable-core render boundary from decision 024 (which made exactly this reversal cheap). The 'Ghostty/Alacritty-class' goal now means class-equivalent FEATURES AND BEHAVIOR, achieved by adopting proven emulation correctness — native means embedded coherently, not homegrown. Next governance pass: amend decision 024 accordingly (owner ratification packet), rewrite the epic phases (jzv.3-.6 obsolete as specified — replace with adapter/integration/feature phases under the new acceptance contract), narrow TF-01, add the screen-authority + canary Phase-0 tasks, restructure the frontier to match. Nothing builds until the owner dispositions the amendment packet.

title: T1a: Replace terminal transport with portable-pty
description: Replace the unsafe hand-rolled PTY with portable-pty while preserving controlling-terminal behavior, independent sessions, process groups/signals, resize, exit status, cwd/environment, inherited credentials, and Datum bootstrap context. Transport remains independent of the selected TerminalCore. Governed by decision 027 and DATUM_NATIVE_TERMINAL_SPEC.
acceptance_criteria: 1. portable-pty owns allocation/spawn/read/write/resize. 2. Process groups and Ctrl-C/terminate behavior pass real pipeline tests. 3. Multiple sessions remain independent. 4. Datum context/env injection and arbitrary executable/argv work. 5. No terminal cell semantics live in the transport.

title: T1b: Integrate the mature TerminalCore adapter
description: Pin and integrate libghostty-vt as the production TerminalCore behind a narrow Datum-owned adapter for PTY feed/replies, resize, render/damage state, selection coordinates, scrollback/search, modes, title/CWD/bell, hyperlinks and graphics. A pinned alacritty_terminal adapter is allowed only by recorded integration failure and equivalent capability evidence. Do not continue the bespoke string/RLE parser into a homegrown grid/reflow core. Governed by decision 027 and DATUM_NATIVE_TERMINAL_SPEC.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pinned libghostty-vt builds reproducibly and its license/provenance are recorded. 2. TerminalCore is closed and vendor structures do not leak into engine/gui-protocol. 3. Adapter drives a deterministic VT/render snapshot corpus. 4. Any fallback is evidence-gated and owner-approved. 5. The old core is not extended as a rival implementation.

title: T2: Complete native renderer, focus, input, IME and text interaction
description: Replace the bespoke TerminalLaneState string/RLE emulator with the selected TerminalCore and adapt its render state to Datum wgpu/text primitives. Complete lossless attributes/color, Unicode/font/fallback/scale behavior, cursor/damage, focus, keyboard, IME, mouse arbitration, selection, clipboard and accessibility foundation. Delete rival legacy screen/parser/input state only after parity evidence. Governed by decision 027 and DATUM_NATIVE_TERMINAL_SPEC.
acceptance_criteria: 1. NT-CAP-02 through NT-CAP-08 and accessibility foundation pass. 2. Render state is lossless and clipped to the terminal cell rectangle. 3. Focus/input/IME/mouse/selection work through one authority. 4. Old screen/parser/RLE and line-editor rivals are removed after parity. 5. Source-health gates and focused real-app tests pass.

title: T3a: Deliver scrollback, reflow, search, links and daily-driver session UX
description: Deliver the native daily-driver surface over TerminalCore: configurable scrollback and reflow, search, hyperlinks/path hints, tabs, splits, profiles/themes/fonts, cwd-aware sessions, lifecycle/close/kill/restart/attach/detach, maximized terminal mode, bell/activity indication outside cells, and shell/TERM/terminfo integration. OSC 7 cwd and OSC 133 prompt/command boundaries are permitted only as untrusted presentation metadata; they never authorize Datum operations. Governed by decisions 027 and 028 plus DATUM_NATIVE_TERMINAL_SPEC and DATUM_TERMINAL_AGENT_INTEROP_SPEC.
acceptance_criteria: 1. NT-CAP-09 through NT-CAP-15 session/UX portions pass. 2. Search and selection remain correct while output and resize occur. 3. Tabs/splits have independent PTY/core state. 4. Profiles/themes/font zoom and cwd-aware new sessions work. 5. Lifecycle semantics are explicit and owner-reviewed. 6. OSC 7/133 metadata improves only cwd/session presentation and cannot trigger, approve, or infer a Datum operation.

title: T3b: Complete modern protocols, graphics, security and accessibility
description: Close the modern terminal ceiling required by decision 027: synchronized output, OSC 8, controlled OSC 52, kitty keyboard, terminal notifications/progress where supported, kitty graphics and sixel through the mature core, bounded image/history memory, paste/link/clipboard/process security policy, and complete accessibility behavior. Governed by decision 027 and DATUM_NATIVE_TERMINAL_SPEC.
acceptance_criteria: 1. NT-CAP-12, NT-CAP-13, NT-CAP-16 and NT-CAP-18 pass. 2. Protocol support has exact fixtures and honest deltas. 3. OSC 52, links, paste and process closing enforce reviewed policy. 4. Graphics are bounded, clipped, scroll/resize-correct and disableable. 5. Screen-reader, keyboard-only, contrast and reduced-motion evidence pass.

title: T4e: Verify full terminal and agent interoperability
description: Close the full native-terminal epic only after T4a-T4d and the terminal capability phases close and a checked-in compatibility matrix proves Datum context refresh, datum-eda, standard authenticated MCP, Codex, Claude Code, a Cursor-compatible CLI when available, a local-agent TUI, named shells/TUIs, vttest/esctest2, Unicode, protocols, security, accessibility, latency, throughput, memory, resize and multi-session behavior on a production Datum build. Governed by decisions 027 and 028 plus both terminal product specifications.
acceptance_criteria: 1. T4a through T4d are closed with product evidence; documentation-only or mocked-terminal proof is insufficient. 2. NT-CAP-17 and every remaining NT-CAP row pass. 3. The checked-in matrix records exact adapter/core versions, commands, results, artifacts and core revision. 4. vttest/esctest2 and known deltas are quantified. 5. Real shell/TUI/agent launch, native MCP discovery, pinned-context, proposal, review, apply, refresh, resume and teardown paths pass. 6. Performance, security, accessibility and visual gates pass. 7. Owner hands-on acceptance passes. 8. Only this slice may close the terminal epic.

title: Align roadmap, tracker, and project-status tooling
description: Create one machine-checkable project-management contract that makes the Active Frontier, beads dependencies/status, live claims, governing documents, and next-task answer consistent. Preserve decision-022 source-health and burn-down enforcement; add hermetic consistency tests and required drift-gate wiring.

Stale claims, state/dependency contradictions, roadmap orphans, and ambiguous ordering fail a blocking checker. 4. Current records are reconciled. 5. description: Render the read-only marking-menu/context-menu shell from menu_model.json with governed layout, icons, disabled not-built/mutating items, and no operation invocation.

The selector validates tracker/claim state but omits it from output. Emit tracker status, assignee, and live-claim state in text and JSON, and prohibit agents from supplementing selector state with conversational memory.

Agents are instructed not to supplement or contradict selector state from conversational memory. 4. Hermetic regressions cover claimed and unclaimed output. 5. Project-state and source-health gates pass.

description: Decision 025 deterministically selects the next task but does not canonically encode the complete steps required to finish it. Add validated structured completion plans and a deterministic task-details query so Claude and Codex cannot omit controlling-spec requirements or infer post-completion ordering.

DP-C02: Completion contracts encode verbatim presentation, fixed order/numbering, no regrouping, and no supplementation. DP-C03: Human and JSON details expose the same execution and presentation policies. DP-C04: Claude and Codex instructions require stdout byte-for-byte for ordinary completion-step queries. title: Dimension rendering + selection re-entry (OPEN-10 deferral; rides decision-020 documentation-system pass)
description: RE-ENTRY TRACKER for the OPEN-10 ratified deferral (S5-C01A owner gate, 2026-08-14): board dimensions are a DELIBERATE EXCLUSION from S5A selection — not a completed capability. Today the engine type (crates/engine/src/board/dimension.rs) is never projected into any scene: not rendered, no primitive, no object_kind, no hit region; the Rendering Book defines no dimension visual construction. EXACT RE-ENTRY CONDITIONS (both required): (1) the Rendering Book defines the dimension visual construction (extension lines, dimension line, arrowheads, text placement); (2) typed scene projection + hit identity exist for dimensions. Expected vehicle: the decision-020 paper-space/viewports documentation-system spec pass (docs/decisions/PRODUCT_MECHANICS_020_PAPER_SPACE_AND_VIEWPORTS.md), which may re-home dimensions in paper space — dimension selection rules must be authored THERE, then reconciled into the UVT S5 matrix (DATUM_UNIVERSAL_VIEWPORT_TOOLING_SPEC.md 2.2.16 dimension row + register OPEN-10). Candidate rules preserved in the register: path rule for extension/dimension lines + oriented-rect for dimension text; measured value derived, never written back.

title: Hierarchical-sheet interaction + selection re-entry (OPEN-11 deferral; rides schematic-surface design pass)
description: RE-ENTRY TRACKER for the OPEN-11 ratified deferral (S5-C01A owner gate, 2026-08-14): hierarchical-sheet interaction and selection are a DELIBERATE EXCLUSION from S5A — not a completed capability. Sheets render today as untyped schematic_graphic rects (id schematic-sheet-instance:{uuid}, schematic_scene_import/mod.rs:293-310) with no hit kind and no typed identity; sheet bodies are visible-but-inert in read-only S5A and the Sheets panel provides list navigation. BINDING GESTURE RESERVATION (already ratified): double-click on a sheet body is reserved for descend-into-sheet; no future step may bind it otherwise. EXACT RE-ENTRY CONDITIONS (both required): (1) the schematic-surface design pass (Active Frontier step 1 remaining scope: schematic editor surface definition) defines the sheet visual construction AND the descend/breadcrumb navigation model; (2) typed sheet + sheet-pin scene authority exists. Open design questions the re-entry must answer: are sheet pins children (symbol-pin analogy)? cross-sheet instance identity (same sheet definition placed twice — definition-vs-instance per OPEN-6 law). Then reconcile into the UVT S5 matrix (2.2.16 sheet row + register OPEN-11). Candidate rules preserved in the register: filled-graphic-style rect qualification for the sheet body with sheet pins as children. NOTE: hierarchy is NOT deferred generally — Global Net resolves across sheets and the semantic Bus spans the hierarchy; only the sheet symbol as a selectable object is deferred.

title: Viewport full-screen ladder: pane Zoom surfaces + Full-Screen Stage (decision 021 amendment)
description: Build rider on the landed P2.1 pane-zoom substrate, specified by the owner-directed 2026-08-14 amendment to decision 021 (PRODUCT_MECHANICS_021 'Full-Screen Stage'). Two-tier maximum-working-space ladder, universal for every pane content (board/schematic/footprint/symbol/model-space/paper-space) by construction: Tier 1 Zoom (pane fills workspace; LANDED mechanism, needs its invocation surfaces) and Tier 2 Full-Screen Stage (pane fills the entire application window, ALL chrome hidden; NEW). Deliver the three invocation surfaces: pane-header maximize button (click = Zoom, Shift+click = Stage), hotkeys Shift+F11 = Zoom / F11 = Stage (entries + shortcuts already in menu_model.json, gate green), View menu entries (view.pane_zoom / view.fullscreen_stage gui-local verbs). Laws: consumer/workspace view state over the unchanged tile tree, exact layout round-trip, never journaled; Escape ordering gesture > Stage > selection (defers to S5 contract); Stage never changes engine state/camera/selection; orthogonal to OS fullscreen.

title: Course-correct the full native terminal product contract
description: Replace the terminal-lite Phase 0 framing with a governed production contract for a fully fledged Datum-native terminal: PTY-only screen truth, mature emulator core adoption, complete daily-driver UX and modern protocols, safe Datum CLI/MCP/agent integration, measurable compatibility/conformance, and deterministic Frontier/tracker sequencing. Preserve decision-022 source-health governance.

description: Provide a standard MCP stdio broker over the Datum daemon, optional secured loopback Streamable HTTP, typed tools, stable datum:// resources, subscriptions where negotiated, and user-invoked portable prompts. A custom endpoint environment variable alone is not acceptance.

AI-MCP-03: Tools, stable datum:// resources, templates, change notifications/subscriptions where negotiated and user-invoked prompts are capability-declared. AI-MCP-04: All supported agents discover the broker through their native project/session configuration; DATUM_MCP_ENDPOINT alone does not satisfy acceptance.

description: Separate live GUI context from immutable pinned work context; require context_id and expected_model_revision fences on proposal/apply; add inspect/propose/apply-approved capability profiles and short-lived session-scoped credentials without secrets in discovery files.
acceptance_criteria: AI-CTX-01: Live GUI context and immutable pinned work context are distinct. AI-CTX-02: Proposal/apply carries context_id and expected_model_revision and stale state refuses or rebases explicitly. AI-CTX-03: Inspect, propose, apply-approved and explicitly enabled unattended capability profiles are session/project scoped. AI-CTX-04: Credentials are short-lived, revocable and absent from tracked discovery/telemetry; audit/journal provenance retains agent/session identity.

AI-WF-02: Thin AGENTS/CLAUDE/Cursor/local projections are generated or parity-validated from one inventory. AI-WF-03: OSC 7/133 shell metadata improves cwd/command UX but never creates design authority or screen-scraped operations.
